hints.content:
###The strategy

$\text{Area of a rectangle} = \text{base} \cdot \text{height}$

Before we can apply the formula to find the area of rectangle $ABCD$, we must find the base and height of the rectangle using the Pythagorean theorem (or the distance formula).

* The base is the length $BC$.
* The height is the length $AB$.

###Step 1: Find the length $BC$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} 
BC^2&= {\redE{1}^2 +\redE{4}^2 }  &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
BC&= \sqrt{\redE{1}^2 +\redE{4}^2 }  &&\text{Square root both sides}\\\\
&=\tealE{\sqrt{17}}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Rectangle A B C D has point A at negative four, five, point B at negative two, negative three, point C at two, negative two, and point D at zero, six. A triangle is formed at point B at negative two, negative three, point C at two, negative two, and a point at two, negative three. The short leg is one unit. The longer leg is four units.

hints.content:
###Step 2: Find the length $AB$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} 
AB^2&= \redE{2}^2 +\redE{8}^2  &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
AB&= \sqrt{\redE{2}^2 +\redE{8}^2 } &&\text{Square root both sides} \\\\
&=\sqrt{68} \\\\
&=\sqrt{4 \cdot 17} \\\\
&=\goldE{2\sqrt{17}}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Rectangle A B C D has point A at negative four, five, point B at negative two, negative three, point C at two, negative two, and point D at zero, six. A triangle is formed at point A at negative four, five, point B at negative two, negative three, and a point at negative four, negative three. The short leg is two units. The longer leg is eight units.

hints.content:
###Step 3: Find the area of the rectangle

Using the base and height of rectangle $ABCD$, we can find the area:

$\begin{align} \text{Area of a rectangle} &= \text{base} \cdot \text{height}\\\\
&= BC\cdot AB \\\\
&= (\tealE{\sqrt{17}})\cdot(\goldE{2\sqrt{17}}) \\\\
&= 2\cdot\sqrt{17}\cdot\sqrt{17} \\\\
&= 2\cdot17 \\\\
&= 34
\end{align}$

###The answer:

The area of rectangle $ABCD$ is $34$ units$^2$.

[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
Yes, we can find the area of the outer rectangle, then subtract the areas of the triangular regions outside of rectangle $ABCD$.



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_{ABCD} &= 6(9) - \text{Area}_{\triangle1} - \text{Area}_{\triangle2} - \text{Area}_{\triangle3} - \text{Area}_{\triangle4} \\\\
&=54 - \dfrac{1}{2}(2)(8)-\dfrac{1}{2}(4)(1)-\dfrac{1}{2}(2)(8)-\dfrac{1}{2}(4)(1)\\\\
&=54-8-2-8-2\\\\
&=34
\end{align}$

The area of rectangle $ABCD$ is $34$ units$^2$.
options.showPrompt: Could we find the area another way?

Rectangle A B C D is inscribed in another rectangle that has a point at negative four, six, a point at negative four, negative three, a point at two, negative three, and a point at two, six. This creates four triangles that are cut out of the larger rectangle by rectangle A B C D. The bottom left triangle is triangle one. The top left triangle is triangle two. The top right triangle is triangle three. The bottom right triangle is triangle four.
